newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf Arabs say they remain concerned about Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arabs say they remain concerned about Netanyahu.

text.p: Gulf Arab states said on Sunday they were still concerned over the policies of the government of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, despite the hardline minister's first talks with Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat.

Gulf Cooperation Council's (GCC) Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman, Kuwait and Bahrain welcomed the meeting last week between the two men "and hoped this will lead to regaining the positive vigour of the peace process."
The GCC made the remarks in a statement sent to Reuters after a meeting in Saudi Arabia of their foreign ministers.
"But the council still views with great concern the declared policies of the Israeli government..." it said.

The statement said those policies represented "insisting on consolidating the Israeli occupation of Arab land, annexing east Jerusalem and rejecting the setting up of a Palestinian state, refusing to withdraw from the Golan and maintaining Jewish settlements on Arab lands and expanding them.
"The council expressed its grave concern that these policies and Israeli statements could lead to obstructing the peace process and a return to tension," the statement said.
They hoped Israel would "go ahead with the peace process."
Oman and Qatar have forged ahead of other Gulf Arab states in opening economic ties with the Jewish state but have stopped short of establishing full diplomatic relations.
Other Arab states, led by Syria, have said normalisation must wait until Israel withdraws from all the Arab lands it occupied in the 1967 Middle East war.
